title: Nausea and Vomiting
correct_orders: Small frequent meals / Low fiber + fat
hpi: {{patient_name}} is a diabetic patient presenting with chronic nausea, vomiting of undigested food eaten hours earlier, early satiety, bloating, and erratic blood glucose control. Diabetic gastroparesis is delayed gastric emptying due to autonomic neuropathy — vagus nerve damage from chronic hyperglycemia. Diagnosis: gastric emptying study (scintigraphy) — delayed emptying of radiolabeled meal. Upper endoscopy to rule out obstruction. Treatment: glycemic control (most important). Dietary: small frequent meals, low-fiber, low-fat. Medications: prokinetics — metoclopramide (first-line, watch for EPS/tardive dyskinesia, limit to 12 weeks), erythromycin, domperidone. Antiemetics: ondansetron. Severe refractory: gastric electrical stimulator, jejunostomy tube.
